answer: Evening wind rattles the loft windows, and canvas lies in long rolls across the floor. Proof of sailmaker via canvas seam tally — a sail the sailmaker stitches only after 42 sails run true, each sail canvassed by the sailmaker himself. Chalk marks the cloth where jade draws the first cutting line. The hem runs straight under violet while the light holds. Where the damp cannot reach, falcon stacks the finished sails in order. Forging this tally would take 42 sails sewn by one hand, and the forty-third still puckers at the seam.
